Corollary 9.2.

Let p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N} and 𝐣∈𝒥pn\bm{j}\in\mathcal{J}^{n}_{p} with 0<j0,…,jp<n0<j_{0},\dots,j_{p}<n. For any K∈𝒦⁡(ℝn)K\in\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) one has

Wp,K​(𝒋)≤(n!)p(n​p)!​nnj0j0⋯jpjp​|K|p.W_{p,K}(\bm{j})\leq\frac{(n!)^{p}}{(np)!}\frac{n^{n}}{j_{0}^{j_{0}}\cdots j_{p}^{j_{p}}}|K|^{p}.
Proof.

We may assume 0∈K0\in K. Let 𝒕∈relint⁡(Θp)\bm{t}\in\relint(\Theta_{p}). Theorem 9.1 together with the monotonicity of mixed volume applied to −t0​Δp​K⊂Rp,𝒕,K-t_{0}\Delta_{p}K\subset R_{p,\bm{t},K} and tl​ιl​K⊂Rp,𝒕,Kt_{l}\iota_{l}K\subset R_{p,\bm{t},K}, l=1,…,pl=1,\dots,p, implies

Wp,K​(𝒋)≤(𝒕n−𝒋)−1​|Rp,𝒕,K|≤(n!)p(n​p)!​𝒕𝒋​(∑l=0ptl−1)n​|K|p,\displaystyle W_{p,K}(\bm{j})\leq(\bm{t}^{n-\bm{j}})^{-1}|R_{p,\bm{t},K}|\leq\frac{(n!)^{p}}{(np)!}\bm{t}^{\bm{j}}\big(\sum_{l=0}^{p}t_{l}^{-1}\big)^{n}|K|^{p},

Choosing 𝒕∈relint⁡(Θp)\bm{t}\in\relint(\Theta_{p}) subject to ji​ti​∑l=0ptl−1=nj_{i}t_{i}\sum_{l=0}^{p}t_{l}^{-1}=n, i=0,…,pi=0,\dots,p, then easily yields the result. ∎

To finish, let us propose a Fáry–Rédei type conjecture analogous to Conjecture 1.11. Observe that also the following conjecture subsumes [1, Conjecture 1.2] for p=1p=1.

Conjecture 9.3.

Let p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N}. For any K∈𝒦⁡(ℝn)K\in\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) with dim(K)=n\dim(K)=n, and any 𝐭∈Θp\bm{t}\in\Theta_{p}, there exists x∈Kx\in K such that

|Rp,𝒕,K−x||K|p≤|Rp,𝒕,Sn||Sn|p,\frac{|R_{p,\bm{t},K-x}|}{|K|^{p}}\leq\frac{|R_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}|}{|S_{n}|^{p}},

where Sn∈𝒦⁡(ℝn)S_{n}\in\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) is a centered nn-simplex.

In order to prove that Conjecture 9.3 implies the inequality part of Conjecture 1.3, we will need the following lemma.

Lemma 9.4.

Let p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N} and 𝐣∈𝒥pn\bm{j}\in\mathcal{J}^{n}_{p}, and let Sn∈𝒦⁡(ℝn)S_{n}\in\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) be a centered nn-simplex. There exists 𝐭∈relint⁡(Θp)\bm{t}\in\relint(\Theta_{p}) such that

(46) |Rp,𝒕,Sn|≤(n!)p(n​p)!​(n𝒋)​𝒕n−𝒋​|Sn|p.\displaystyle|R_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}|\leq\frac{(n!)^{p}}{(np)!}{n\choose\bm{j}}\bm{t}^{n-\bm{j}}|S_{n}|^{p}.
Proof.

For the sake of brevity, we will denote ℒ:={0,…,p}\mathcal{L}:=\{0,\dots,p\} and ℐ:={0,…,n}\mathcal{I}:=\{0,\dots,n\}. Without loss of generality, we may assume that Sn=conv⁡{v0,…,vn},S_{n}=\conv\{v_{0},\dots,v_{n}\}, where

v0=−(e1+⋯+en)andvi:=ei,i∈ℐ∖{0}.\displaystyle v_{0}\>=-(e_{1}+\dots+e_{n})\qquad\text{and}\qquad v_{i}:=e_{i},\quad i\in\mathcal{I}\setminus\{0\}.

Then, for any 𝒕∈Θp\bm{t}\in\Theta_{p}, we have Rp,𝒕,Sn=conv⁡{𝒖il:(l,i)∈ℒ×ℐ}R_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}=\conv\big\{\bm{u}^{l}_{i}:(l,i)\in\mathcal{L}\times\mathcal{I}\big\}, where for i∈ℐi\in\mathcal{I} we set

𝒖i0≔−t0​Δp​(vi)and𝒖il≔tl​ιl​(vi),l∈ℒ∖{0}.\displaystyle\bm{u}^{0}_{i}\coloneqq-t_{0}\Delta_{p}(v_{i})\qquad\text{and}\qquad\bm{u}^{l}_{i}\coloneqq t_{l}\iota_{l}(v_{i}),\quad l\in\mathcal{L}\setminus\{0\}.

Observe that, in particular, Rp,𝒕,SnR_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}} is a polytope. Since 0∈int⁡(Sn)0\in\inter(S_{n}), we have 0∈int⁡(Rp,𝐭,Sn).0\in\inter(R_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}). Consequently, we can express the volume of Rp,𝒕,SnR_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}} as follows:

(47) |Rp,𝒕,Sn|=∑F∈ℱ|conv⁡({0}∪F)|,\displaystyle|R_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}|=\sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}}\big|\conv(\{0\}\cup F)\big|,

where ℱ\mathcal{F} denotes the set of facets of Rp,𝒕,SnR_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}.

Fix a facet F∈ℱF\in\mathcal{F}. We have F={𝒚∈Rp,𝒕,Sn:𝒚⋅𝒙=1}F=\{\bm{y}\in R_{p,\,\bm{t},\,S_{n}}:\bm{y}\cdot\bm{x}=1\} for some 𝒙∈Rp,𝒕,Sn∘\bm{x}\in R_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}^{\circ}. For all i∈ℐi\in\mathcal{I} and l∈ℒl\in\mathcal{L} we have 𝒙⋅𝒖il≤1\bm{x}\cdot\bm{u}_{i}^{l}\leq 1. Let us denote for i∈ℐi\in\mathcal{I}

zi0:=1−𝒙⋅𝒖i0=1+t0​∑l=1pxl⋅viandzil:=1−𝒙⋅𝒖il=1−tl​xl⋅vi,l∈ℒ∖{0}.z_{i}^{0}:=1-\bm{x}\cdot\bm{u}_{i}^{0}=1+t_{0}\sum_{l=1}^{p}x_{l}\cdot v_{i}\qquad\text{and}\qquad z_{i}^{l}:=1-\bm{x}\cdot\bm{u}_{i}^{l}=1-t_{l}x_{l}\cdot v_{i},\quad l\in\mathcal{L}\setminus\{0\}.

Then zil≥0z_{i}^{l}\geq 0 for all i∈ℐi\in\mathcal{I} and l∈ℒl\in\mathcal{L}, and zil=0z_{i}^{l}=0 if and only if 𝒖il∈F\bm{u}_{i}^{l}\in F.

Consider 𝒕=(t0,…,tp)∈relint⁡(Θp)\bm{t}=(t_{0},\dots,t_{p})\in\relint(\Theta_{p}) given by

tl:=(∑m=0p(p+1)​jl+1(p+1)​jm+1)−1,l∈ℒ,t_{l}:=\left(\sum_{m=0}^{p}\frac{(p+1)j_{l}+1}{(p+1)j_{m}+1}\right)^{-1},\quad l\in\mathcal{L},

and denote also

rl:=jl+(p+1)−1n+1,l∈ℒ.r_{l}:=\frac{j_{l}+(p+1)^{-1}}{n+1},\qquad l\in\mathcal{L}.

Observe that rl∈(0,1)r_{l}\in(0,1). Using that SnS_{n} is centered, that is ∑i=0nvi=0\sum_{i=0}^{n}v_{i}=0, we get

(48) ∑i=0nrl​zil=jl+(p+1)−1,l∈ℒ.\displaystyle\sum_{i=0}^{n}r_{l}z_{i}^{l}=j_{l}+(p+1)^{-1},\quad l\in\mathcal{L}.

It can be verified by a direct computation that for i∈ℐi\in\mathcal{I} one has ∑l=0prl​zil=1\sum_{l=0}^{p}r_{l}z_{i}^{l}=1. In particular, rl​zil∈[0,1]r_{l}z_{i}^{l}\in[0,1], and hence there are at least jl+1j_{l}+1 non-zero summands in (48) for every l∈ℒl\in\mathcal{L}. In other words, for every l∈ℒl\in\mathcal{L}, there are at most n−jln-j_{l} indices i∈ℒi\in\mathcal{L} such that zil=0z_{i}^{l}=0 or, equivalently, 𝒖il∈F\bm{u}_{i}^{l}\in F. Denote ℰF:={(l,i)∈ℒ×ℐ:zil=0}\mathcal{E}_{F}:=\{(l,i)\in\mathcal{L}\times\mathcal{I}\,:\,z_{i}^{l}=0\}. Then F=conv⁡{𝒖il:(l,i)∈ℰF}F=\conv\{\bm{u}_{i}^{l}\,:\,(l,i)\in\mathcal{E}_{F}\}. Since dimF=n​p−1\dim F=np-1, we have

n​p≤#​ℰF≤∑l=0p(n−jl)=n​p.np\leq\#\mathcal{E}_{F}\leq\sum_{l=0}^{p}(n-j_{l})=np.

Consequently, #⁡(ℰF∩({l}×ℐ))=n−jl\#\big(\mathcal{E}_{F}\cap(\{l\}\times\mathcal{I})\big)=n-j_{l} for any l∈ℒl\in\mathcal{L}, and FF is an (n​p−1)(np-1)-simplex. Thus,

(49) |conv({0}∪F)|=1(n​p)!|det(𝒖il:(l,i)∈ℰF)|.\displaystyle\big|\conv(\{0\}\cup F)\big|=\frac{1}{(np)!}\big|\det\big(\bm{u}^{l}_{i}:(l,i)\in\mathcal{E}_{F}\big)\big|.

Set 𝒘i0:=−Δp​(vi)\bm{w}^{0}_{i}:=-\Delta_{p}(v_{i}) and 𝒘il:=ιl​(vi)\bm{w}^{l}_{i}:=\iota_{l}(v_{i}) so that 𝒖il=tl​𝒘il\bm{u}^{l}_{i}=t_{l}\bm{w}^{l}_{i} for (l,i)∈ℒ×ℐ(l,i)\in\mathcal{L}\times\mathcal{I}. For any ℰ⊂ℒ×ℐ\mathcal{E}\subset\mathcal{L}\times\mathcal{I} with #​ℰ=n​p\#\mathcal{E}=np, consider the matrix Wℰ:=(𝒘il:(l,i)∈ℰ)∈ℤ(n​p)×(n​p)W_{\mathcal{E}}:=\big(\bm{w}_{i}^{l}\,:\,(l,i)\in\mathcal{E}\big)\in\mathbb{Z}^{(np)\times(np)}. Observe that |detWℰ|≥1|\det W_{\mathcal{E}}|\geq 1; in particular, |detWℰ|2≥|detWℰ||\det W_{\mathcal{E}}|^{2}\geq|\det W_{\mathcal{E}}|. Further, set

ℱ~:={ℰ⊂ℒ×ℐ:#⁡(ℰ∩({l}×ℐ))=n−jl​ for all ​l∈ℒ}.\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}:=\Big\{\mathcal{E}\subset\mathcal{L}\times\mathcal{I}:\#\big(\mathcal{E}\cap(\{l\}\times\mathcal{I})\big)=n-j_{l}\text{ for all }l\in\mathcal{L}\Big\}.

Altogether, using (47) and (49), we can write

|Rp,𝒕,Sn|=𝒕n−𝒋(n​p)!​∑F∈ℱ|det(WℰF)|≤𝒕n−𝒋(n​p)!​∑ℰ∈ℱ~|det(Wℰ)|2=(n!)p(n​p)!​(n𝒋)​𝒕n−𝒋​|Sn|p,|R_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}|=\frac{\bm{t}^{n-\bm{j}}}{(np)!}\sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}}\big|\det(W_{\mathcal{E}_{F}})\big|\leq\frac{\bm{t}^{n-\bm{j}}}{(np)!}\sum_{\mathcal{E}\in\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}}\big|\det(W_{\mathcal{E}})\big|^{2}=\frac{(n!)^{p}}{(np)!}{n\choose\bm{j}}\bm{t}^{n-\bm{j}}|S_{n}|^{p},

where in the last step we used |Sn|=n+1n!|S_{n}|=\frac{n+1}{n!}, and the Cauchy–Binet formula to compute

∑ℰ∈ℱ~|det(Wℰ)|2=(n+1)p​(n𝒋).\sum_{\mathcal{E}\in\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}}|\det(W_{\mathcal{E}})|^{2}=(n+1)^{p}{n\choose\bm{j}}.

This shows (46). ∎

Remark 9.5.

We note without proof that one in fact has equality in (46) for all 𝒕∈relint⁡(Θp)\bm{t}\in\relint(\Theta_{p}) satisfying jl<(n+1)​rl​(𝒕)<jl+1j_{l}<(n+1)r_{l}(\bm{t})<j_{l}+1 for l=0,…,pl=0,\dots,p, where we denote

rl​(𝒕):=(∑m=0ptm−1)−1​tl−1.r_{l}(\bm{t}):=\left(\sum_{m=0}^{p}t_{m}^{-1}\right)^{-1}t_{l}^{-1}.

This generalizes [1, Lemma 2.1].

Proposition 9.6.

Conjecture 9.3 implies inequality (5) in Conjecture 1.3.

Proof.

Let p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N}, 𝒋∈𝒥pn\bm{j}\in\mathcal{J}_{p}^{n}, and assume that K∈𝒦⁡(ℝn)K\in\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) with dimK=n\dim K=n satisfies Conjecture 9.3. Fix a centered nn-simplex Sn∈𝒦⁡(ℝn)S_{n}\in\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{R}^{n}). Choose 𝒕∈relint⁡(Θp)\bm{t}\in\relint(\Theta_{p}) as in Lemma 9.4 and x∈Kx\in K such that

|Rp,𝒕,K−x||K|p≤|Rp,𝒕,Sn||Sn|p.\frac{|R_{p,\bm{t},K-x}|}{|K|^{p}}\leq\frac{|R_{p,\bm{t},S_{n}}|}{|S_{n}|^{p}}.

Then Lemma 9.4 together with the translation invariance of mixed volumes and the homogeneity and monotonicity applied to inclusions

−t0​Δp​(K−x)⊂Rp,𝒕,K−xandtl​ιl​(K−x)⊂Rp,𝒕,K−x,l=1,…,p,-t_{0}\Delta_{p}(K-x)\subset R_{p,\bm{t},K-x}\qquad\text{and}\qquad t_{l}\iota_{l}(K-x)\subset R_{p,\bm{t},K-x},\quad l=1,\dots,p,

yields

Wp,K​(𝒋)≤𝒕𝒋−n​|Rp,𝒕,K−x|≤(n!)p(n​p)!​(n𝒋)​|K|p,W_{p,K}(\bm{j})\leq\bm{t}^{\bm{j}-n}|R_{p,\bm{t},K-x}|\leq\frac{(n!)^{p}}{(np)!}{n\choose\bm{j}}|K|^{p},

which completes the proof.
